newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sentrachem, Bayer plant gets go ahead.
newsitem.headline: Sentrachem, Bayer plant gets go ahead.

text.p: Sentrachem Ltd and German chemicals group Bayer AG said on Thursday that work would soon begin on the 510 million rand chrome chemicals facility in Newcastle in KwaZulu-Natal province.
The venture, announced on February 21 this year, will result in one of the world's largest chrome chemicals facilities.

Both companies have a 50 percent shareholding in the project which will annually produce 70,000 tons of sodium dichromate and 10,000 tons of chromic acid, used in the leather tanning, pigments, metal treatment and associated industries.
About 95 percent of the production would be exported to the Pacific Rim, Europe and North America either directly or after local beneficiation, the statement said.
About 1,200 people would be employed during construction and 100 full time positions would be created.
